Maritime NDT training in Bath, Maine: the short answer

Maritime NDT training for Bath and Midcoast Maine employers is delivered by Atlantis NDT as live online classes or onsite at your facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A and cover the methods destroyer construction and its supply chain rely on: VT, MT, UT, PAUT, RT and PT on welded steel structure and piping. Navy work adds NAVSEA qualification inside the employer's programme. Atlantis has no training centre in Maine; quotes are on request.

Bath is a one-shipyard town with a national footprint. General Dynamics Bath Iron Works builds the Navy's Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers and built the Zumwalt class, and its demand for welders, fitters and examiners shapes the whole Midcoast labour market. Around it sit a fabrication and supplier base, the Navy's public submarine yard at Kittery, a long coast of commercial and yacht builders, and industrial plants that also need certified examiners. This page explains how NDT training and certification work for that market, honestly, including what Atlantis can and cannot do for you.

To start, request a maritime NDT training quote for Bath, Maine.

Shipbuilding NDT work in Bath and Midcoast Maine

Destroyer construction at Bath Iron Works

Destroyers are built in units and grand blocks in the yard's fabrication and assembly facilities in Bath and Brunswick, then joined on the land-level construction facility before launch. Each stage produces examination scope: structural welds in the panel and unit lines, erection joints where blocks come together, foundations for combat systems and machinery, and miles of piping in carbon steel, stainless and copper-nickel. The work answers to Navy technical requirements: NAVSEA documents for the NDT methods and personnel qualification, MIL-STD-2035 for acceptance criteria, and fabrication standards for ship structure. A destroyer packs dense systems into a compact hull, so a lot of examination happens in tight spaces against fit-out deadlines.

Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, Kittery

About an hour and a half down the coast, Portsmouth Naval Shipyard in Kittery is a Navy public shipyard that overhauls, repairs and modernises nuclear-powered submarines. Its examiners are certified within the Navy's own programme, and much of its scope is nuclear or submarine-hull work with its own regime. Contractors and suppliers supporting the yard face the same NAVSEA expectations as Bath suppliers. See maritime NDT consulting for the Portsmouth area.

Suppliers and fabricators

Midcoast and southern Maine host machine shops, fabricators and component suppliers serving both yards and the wider naval supply chain. When a supplier first wins Navy-related work, it typically discovers that its customer expects NDT personnel certified under a written practice, procedures that cite the right acceptance standard, and records that a government or prime-contractor auditor can follow.

Commercial, yacht and composite builders

Maine's coast has a long tradition of commercial boatbuilding: workboats, ferries, fishing vessels, research vessels and high-end yachts, increasingly in aluminium and composites. Steel and aluminium builds working to class require VT, MT, PT and UT of welds; composite builders use UT and tap testing for bond and laminate quality. These builders rarely need NAVSEA qualification but do need certified personnel when class or a government customer requires it.

Other industrial work that keeps Maine technicians busy

Maine examiners are rarely confined to one sector. Pulp and paper mills need boiler-tube thickness surveys and pressure-vessel inspections during outages, power and energy facilities require boiler and piping examination, and southern Maine has aerospace manufacturing that works to aerospace NDT requirements, which differ from shipbuilding ones. The site of the decommissioned Maine Yankee plant in Wiscasset, near Bath, continues to store spent fuel; Maine has no operating commercial reactor. A technician with broad SNT-TC-1A certifications can move between these sectors as the yard's workload shifts.

Methods used on shipbuilding work in Bath

MethodShipbuilding application in Bath and Midcoast MaineCode / standard usually invoked
VTFit-up, in-process and final weld inspection in units and blocks; dimensional and profile checksNAVSEA T9074-AS-GIB-010/271; MIL-STD-1689 (surface ship structure); MIL-STD-2035 acceptance
MTFillet and tee welds on ferritic structure, foundations, back-gouge and excavation checksNAVSEA 271; MIL-STD-2035
UTFull-penetration structural welds, erection joints, lamination checks before weldingNAVSEA 271; MIL-STD-2035; AWS D1.1 on non-naval structure
PAUT / TOFDEncoded examination of erection joints and critical welds where the specification permits; reduces radiography downtimeAs permitted by the contract and NAVSEA; ASME Section V on commercial work
RTPiping system welds and specified structural joints needing a permanent imageNAVSEA 271; MIL-STD-2035
PTStainless and copper-nickel piping, aluminium structure on commercial builds, non-magnetic fittingsNAVSEA 271; MIL-STD-2035; class rules
ETSurface crack detection through coatings; heat exchanger tubing in industrial plantsProcedure-specific

Local method spotlight: MT and VT done to Navy acceptance criteria. On a destroyer build, the highest-volume examinations are visual and magnetic particle checks on structural fillet and tee welds. They are not glamorous, but they are where a new technician earns trust: interpreting MIL-STD-2035 criteria correctly, recognising relevant versus non-relevant indications, and recording results so that rework is targeted, not guessed. A Bath technician who has mastered MT Level II and visual inspection then adds UT Level II and phased array to become a volumetric examiner.

The SNT-TC-1A path, step by step, for a Bath technician

  1. Employer written practice: sets training, experience, exams and recertification per method and level; Navy-work employers add NAVSEA provisions.
  2. Classroom training per method, typically VT and MT first, then UT. Use the training requirements matrix for SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.
  3. Documented on-the-job experience under certified supervision, recording joint types, materials and thicknesses.
  4. General, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, the practical on real weld specimens.
  5. Vision examination.
  6. Written certification by the employer.
  7. NAVSEA qualification for Navy scope, via the employer's programme.
  8. Recertification on the interval the written practice sets.

More: SNT-TC-1A training and certification and the Level II path.

Radiation licensing and site access in Maine

Maine is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography with radioactive sources at commercial sites in Maine is licensed through the state's radiation control programme within the Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention, and radiographers must meet the state's training and certification requirements, which follow the federal industrial radiography rules. Work at federal installations under exclusive federal jurisdiction, such as parts of a Navy shipyard, may need NRC reciprocity instead. X-ray equipment is registered separately from radioactive material. Your radiation safety officer confirms which rules apply to each job.

Shipyard and Navy access is a separate gate: yard badges and site training, base-access credentials for government property, and in some roles citizenship or security vetting. Marine terminals regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act, such as those in Portland, require TWIC for unescorted access. Plan those lead times into hiring and training.

How Atlantis delivers maritime NDT training to Bath-area crews

  • Onsite at your facility: an ASNT Level III-led cohort at your shop in Bath, Brunswick or elsewhere in Maine, using your equipment, specimens and procedures. Practical exams and records stay with your company, where auditors expect them.
  • Live online: theory and exam preparation for technicians spread across Midcoast, southern Maine and New Hampshire, which matters in a rural state with long winter drives. See online NDT training.
  • Blended: theory online in the quieter weeks, practical sessions onsite when production allows, scheduled around ship milestones and the weather rather than a fixed public calendar.

Shipbuilding emphasis on request: reading NAVSEA drawings and weld symbols, MIL-STD-2035 acceptance, MT technique on stiffened plate, UT on tee joints, PT on stainless and copper-nickel, and record-keeping for prime-contractor audits. Ask about onsite maritime NDT training for your Bath crew. Multi-site programmes run through corporate NDT training; sector cohorts are described on marine and defense corporate training pages.

Written practices and Level III services for Maine shipbuilding suppliers

A Maine supplier moving into the naval supply chain usually needs to fix its paperwork before it fixes anything else. Common gaps: no written practice, or a template that does not match the methods performed; procedures citing the wrong acceptance standard; untraceable training records; and no defined Level III. Small companies often cannot justify a full-time Level III, which is where outside Level III services help.

  • Written practice development and review to SNT-TC-1A with NAVSEA and class notes: NDT written practice development.
  • Level III services: procedure and technique review, exam development and administration, records audits.
  • Supplier readiness reviews before a customer audit.

Local consulting pages: maritime NDT consulting in Bath, NDT consulting in Bath, Maine and NDT consulting in Brunswick, Maine. To have your documents reviewed, book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator covers 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments, including a welding workshop that maps closely to shipyard weld examination. It is useful for rehearsing MT technique, UT scanning and indication recognition between classes, especially for technicians far from a training venue. It is practice only and does not replace hands-on training or the practical exam on real specimens. Local entry: Practical NDT Bath, Maine.

Local options compared

  • Bath Iron Works with the Maine Community College System: the yard partners with Southern Maine Community College, including courses at its Midcoast campus in Brunswick, on short-term trades training such as a welding academy whose content includes destructive and non-destructive testing. These are hiring pipelines for the yard rather than full NDT certification courses.
  • Bath Iron Works' own training: the yard trains and certifies its examiners under its own programme.
  • Maine Maritime Academy in Castine educates marine engineers and deck officers; useful background for marine careers, not an NDT certification programme.
  • Out-of-state providers: dedicated NDT college programmes and training centres exist elsewhere in New England and beyond; Maine has few local options for full NDT courses.
  • Atlantis NDT: employer cohorts, live online and onsite SNT-TC-1A training, plus written practice and Level III services, which suits Maine's dispersed employers. Not the right choice if you need NAVSEA qualification issued outside an employer's programme.

City- and state-wide views: NDT training in Bath, Maine and NDT training in Maine.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content and practical exams and, where your written practice designates Atlantis as an outside agency, exam administration.

Frequently asked questions about maritime NDT training in Bath, Maine

How do I become an NDT technician at a shipyard in Maine?

Either join the yard through its hiring and training pipelines and progress into inspection, or earn SNT-TC-1A certifications in VT, MT and UT through an employer or training provider and join a supplier or inspection company. NAVSEA qualification for Navy work comes through the employer's programme.

Can I take NDT training online in Maine?

Yes for theory and exam preparation, through live online classes. Practical training and the practical exam must be hands-on; we deliver those onsite at the employer's facility.

Does Atlantis training qualify me for Bath Iron Works?

Atlantis is not affiliated with Bath Iron Works. Our training builds method knowledge an employer can credit, but the yard certifies its own examiners under its programme, and NAVSEA qualification is administered by the employer.

What NDT methods are used most in destroyer construction?

Visual and magnetic particle testing carry the largest volume on structural welds; ultrasonic testing and radiography cover full-penetration and piping welds; penetrant testing covers non-magnetic materials.

Do I need a radiography licence in Maine?

Your employer needs a state radioactive materials licence (Maine is an NRC Agreement State), and you must meet the state's radiographer training and certification requirements. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A method certification.

Is there NDT work in Maine outside shipbuilding?

Yes: paper mill and power plant outages, structural fabrication, commercial boatbuilding and aerospace manufacturing. Aerospace employers usually work to NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A.

How long does it take to get MT or UT Level II?

The employer's written practice sets classroom hours and experience using SNT-TC-1A as the reference; see the training requirements matrix. Practise with UT Level 2 practice questions.

What does maritime NDT training cost in Bath?

Atlantis quotes on request. Cost depends on methods, levels, group size, online or onsite delivery, travel to the site, and any written practice or Level III work. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding?

Those programmes generally require an approved school or listed eligible training provider. Atlantis does not claim that status; check provider lists, or ask about employer-paid training. Veterans can read veterans transitioning into NDT.

Can a welder at the yard move into NDT?

Yes. Welders already understand joints and discontinuities, which shortens the learning curve. See welder to NDT technician without a degree.

Can I train for NDT work at Portsmouth Naval Shipyard?

The public yard in Kittery hires and certifies its own examiners within the Navy's programme, and its contractors certify theirs under their own written practices with NAVSEA provisions. SNT-TC-1A method training is a sound foundation for either route, but the qualification for submarine and nuclear scope is granted by the employer, not by an outside course.

Do composite boatbuilders in Maine need certified NDT technicians?

Some do, particularly when a government customer or a class society requires documented inspection of laminates and bonded joints. Ultrasonic testing is the main method; procedures are usually builder-specific. If your shop is formalising composite inspection, a written practice and Level III-reviewed procedures are the place to start.

How does Bath compare with other US shipbuilding centres?

Bath is destroyer new construction; Newport News builds carriers and submarines; Norfolk is mostly repair; Groton builds submarines. See Newport News, Norfolk and Groton.
